evidence_class: response-open baseline field-design feasibility only; no future TNC or future meadow outcome

planned_diagnostic.predictor: within_node_centered_anchor_TNC = anchor_TNC - mean(anchor_TNC across the three anchors)
planned_diagnostic.outcome: future Thalassia Braun-Blanquet score at the same permanent meter mark; sampled focal absence may be coded 0, present nonnumeric 'Reported' is quantitatively missing
planned_diagnostic.uncertainty: stable-node cluster bootstrap, resampling the full three-anchor node as one unit
planned_diagnostic.role: secondary spatial site-template-resistant diagnostic; cannot replace or rescue the four-bay node-level primary TNC result

interpretation: The four-bay q25/q50/q75 anchor diagnostic is baseline-feasible before any future response: 38 nodes have three distinct Thalassia-positive anchors with quantitative baseline Braun-Blanquet values, exceeding the frozen >=36 total / >=6 per-bay gate.
claim_boundary: This is a baseline design audit, not evidence that TNC predicts future state.
Core anchor positions may not move after TNC assay, environmental measurements, or future outcome access.

Support in the future within-node diagnostic would weaken stable transect-level site-template confounding but would not eliminate persistent meter-mark microhabitat or time-varying local common causes.
If coring may plausibly alter a paired permanent meter mark, that anchor is invalid for the future local diagnostic rather than interpreted ecologically.
